memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user keeps packing tape for returns in an upper kitchen drawer.
The user arrived ten minutes before the post office closed and found that numbered-ticket intake had ended.
Before the next visit, the user checked the operating hours and arrived one hour before closing.
The user went to the counter without closing a return box and had to go back to the packing station.
For the next return, the user sealed the box at home and completed intake in one attempt.
The user scheduled bank and post-office errands for the same day, but they took a long time because the destinations were in different directions.
The following week, after checking the locations on a map, the user visited nearby branches in sequence.
Postal staff expect a return-label barcode to arrive affixed flat, without a fold.
Before grouping errands into one outing, check each institution's location and operating hours that day.
Postal and financial counters may operate on different hours than usual around public holidays.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate practical domains: the reference frame concerns sleep, caffeine, meal fatigue, and bedroom conditions, while the compared frame concerns preparing returns and planning postal, banking, and routing errands. Neither frame contains a counterpart to the other’s claims.

relations.reason: These reference-only memories jointly describe one sleep-environment setup: the fan is beside the window, an open window admitted disruptive noise, and running the fan allowed the window to remain closed without excessive warmth.
relations.summary: A bedside fan and window choices affect bedroom comfort and exposure to street noise.

relations.reason: These reference-only memories split one timing-sensitive caffeine claim across a late-coffee episode, an earlier-coffee contrast, and a broader tendency toward later bedtimes after late-afternoon coffee.
relations.summary: The user’s observed sleep timing varies with how late they drink coffee.

relations.reason: These reference-only observations describe the same underlying pattern of conserving effort around dinner when tired, using either food prepared elsewhere or a simple home meal.
relations.summary: On tired days, low-effort meal choices were followed by immediate rest or postponed chores.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only preference and belief concerning another person, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user’s father wants coffee available after dinner and does not expect it to impair sleep.

relations.reason: This reference-only instruction governs interpretation of sparse sleep observations and has no corresponding evidence-handling policy in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Sleep suggestions should not generalize a lifestyle habit from only one or two records.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories split one return-box preparation claim across tape storage, an unsealed-box failure, and a later one-attempt success after sealing at home.
relations.summary: Keeping packing tape available and sealing a return box at home can prevent a failed counter attempt.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories provide failure and success observations for the same operational decision about when to arrive for postal intake.
relations.summary: Arriving shortly before posted closing may be too late for intake, whereas arriving substantially earlier can avoid that problem.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories split one errand-planning claim across inefficient routing, improved sequencing of nearby branches, and explicit advance-checking guidance.
relations.summary: Grouped errands should account for both branch locations and daily operating hours before the outing.

relations.reason: This compared-only packaging requirement is independently useful and has no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Postal staff expect a return-label barcode to be attached flat and without a fold.

relations.reason: This compared-only holiday-specific scheduling caveat is independently useful and has no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Postal and financial counter hours may differ from their usual schedules around public holidays.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame records return-package preparation, counter-arrival timing, efficient errand routing, barcode placement requirements, and possible holiday-hour changes.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame records caffeine-related sleep timing, bedroom cooling and noise conditions, low-effort meals on tired days, a family coffee preference, and caution against generalizing from sparse observations.
